speaker: Doctor
text: That's a great start. Can you tell me if these spots are itchy, painful, or bleeding? Also, did you notice them appearing in a specific pattern or shape?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the lesions are painless and non-pruritic but appeared in a daycare setting with a recent chickenpox case, could you describe the color and texture of these papules, and have any new spots appeared since the first were noticed? Also, has your child had a fever, cough, or runny nose recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic for this viral infection, which is common in daycare settings. No further tests are needed at this time.
